title: Cryptool vs Sablier
content_html:
Cryptool vs Sablier comes down to whether you need just token vesting or a complete investment operating system. Sablier is an on-chain protocol for token streaming and vesting schedules, built for developers and teams that need programmable payment flows. Cryptool is a multi-chain investment platform that includes token vesting alongside portfolio tracking, fund administration, syndicate management and investor reporting in one non-custodial system.

Pick Sablier if you are a developer integrating vesting into a smart contract, or a project team that needs only token streaming with no surrounding fund operations. Pick Cryptool if you are running a fund, syndicate or investment group where vesting schedules sit alongside portfolio positions, LP allocations and quarterly reporting.

What Sablier is good at

Sablier is an on-chain protocol for streaming tokens and creating vesting schedules. Tokens flow continuously from sender to recipient based on elapsed time, rather than releasing in discrete chunks. This makes it useful for payroll, grants and any situation where a linear release schedule matters.

The protocol is composable, meaning other contracts can integrate it directly. A DAO can set up continuous payment streams for contributors. A project can vest tokens to early backers with no manual intervention. Everything runs on-chain with no intermediary.

Sablier supports multiple EVM chains and has been audited repeatedly. It is open source and non-custodial by design. The contracts hold tokens in escrow and release them according to the schedule encoded at creation. No one can alter the terms once the stream starts.

For teams that need only vesting or streaming and already have their portfolio, fund admin and reporting infrastructure elsewhere, Sablier does exactly what it says and does it well.

What Cryptool does differently

Cryptool is a crypto investment operating system that includes token vesting as one module within a broader platform. The vesting layer works similarly to Sablier in that schedules are configured once and distributions happen automatically. The difference is what sits around it.

A fund manager on cryptool connects wallets non-custodially across all chains, sees portfolio positions in real time, runs capital raises with tiered allocations, sets vesting schedules for those allocations, and generates quarterly LP reports from the same system. The vesting schedule is not isolated: it appears on the investor portal, feeds into performance analytics, and shows up on the shared calendar alongside other fund events.

A syndicate lead running a token round on cryptool tracks the deal pipeline, collects commitments from members, calculates per-member allocations based on tier and commitment size, configures the vesting schedule at the deal level, and distributes tokens automatically at each unlock. Members see their unvested balance, upcoming unlock dates and total position value in the investor portal without asking for a statement.

The platform is non-custodial. Wallets connect read-only for portfolio tracking. On-chain modules run on EVM chains and MultiversX, with more coming. Funds stay in user wallets, and every transaction is signed by the user.

Cryptool also includes an OTC marketplace where locked allocations can be listed and traded before vesting completes, which matters when an investor wants liquidity before the unlock schedule ends. Sablier does not include a marketplace layer.

For a comparison of how cryptool handles multi-chain portfolio tracking alongside fund operations, the portfolio guide covers the setup.

Which one should you pick

Pick Sablier if:

  • You need only token streaming or vesting with no surrounding fund infrastructure
  • You are integrating vesting into a smart contract or dApp
  • You want a composable protocol with no additional layers
  • Your portfolio tracking, fund admin and reporting already live elsewhere

Pick Cryptool if:

  • You are running a fund, syndicate or investment group where vesting is one part of a larger operation
  • You need portfolio tracking, allocation management, investor reporting and vesting in one system
  • You want an investor portal where LPs see their positions and upcoming unlocks without asking for statements
  • You need an OTC marketplace for trading locked allocations before vesting completes
  • You are running capital raises and need tiered allocations with automated vesting and distribution

Pick both if:

  • You want Sablier's on-chain vesting contracts but need Cryptool's fund admin, reporting and portfolio layer on top. The two can work together: vesting happens on-chain via Sablier, and cryptool reads the wallet to track positions and generate reports.

For teams managing investor allocations across multiple wallets, the wallet connection guide covers the setup.

Real-world example

A crypto VC fund invests in multiple projects each year, each deal typically including a vesting schedule with quarterly unlocks over a period of 12 to 36 months. The fund works with a group of LPs who receive quarterly statements showing their allocation across all portfolio companies, including unvested positions.

On Sablier alone, the vesting schedules run on-chain and tokens release automatically. The fund still needs a separate system to track the portfolio, calculate each LP's percentage share of every position, generate quarterly statements, and provide a portal where LPs can check their holdings without emailing the GP.

On Cryptool, the vesting schedules are configured at the deal level, tokens distribute automatically at each unlock, and the positions feed into the portfolio view. The fund manager sees total portfolio value across all chains and all deals. Each LP sees their own allocation, unvested balance and upcoming unlock dates in the investor portal. Quarterly reports generate automatically from the connected wallets. The OTC marketplace lets LPs trade unvested allocations if they need liquidity before the schedule completes.

The difference is not whether vesting works: both handle that. The difference is whether vesting is isolated or integrated into the rest of the fund operation.

For a direct comparison with another vesting-focused platform, see Cryptool vs Hedgey.

FAQ

What is the main difference between cryptool and sablier?

Sablier is an on-chain protocol for token vesting and streaming payments. Cryptool is a crypto investment operating system that includes token vesting alongside multi-chain portfolio tracking, fund administration, syndicate management, capital raising, investor reporting and an OTC marketplace. Sablier does vesting and does it well. Cryptool does vesting as part of a broader platform for managing funds, syndicates and investment groups.

Can I use sablier for vesting and cryptool for everything else?

Yes. Sablier handles the on-chain vesting contracts, and Cryptool connects to the wallets non-custodially to track positions, calculate allocations and generate investor reports. The two are not mutually exclusive. Many fund managers use on-chain vesting protocols for execution and a platform like Cryptool for portfolio tracking, fund admin and reporting.

Does cryptool support the same chains as sablier?

Cryptool supports all chains and all wallet providers for portfolio tracking. On-chain modules, including vesting and distribution, run on EVM chains and MultiversX, with more coming. Sablier runs on multiple EVM chains. For portfolio tracking, Cryptool covers more. For on-chain vesting execution, both support EVM.

Which one is better for a crypto fund?

If the fund needs only vesting and already has portfolio tracking, fund admin and investor reporting handled elsewhere, Sablier is a focused, audited protocol that does exactly that. If the fund needs vesting integrated with portfolio tracking, LP allocations, quarterly reporting and an investor portal in one system, Cryptool is built for that use case. Most crypto funds need the full stack, not just the vesting layer.

Does cryptool have an OTC marketplace for locked allocations?

Yes. Cryptool includes an OTC marketplace where locked allocations can be listed and traded before vesting completes. Buyers see the vesting schedule and remaining lockup period upfront. Settlement happens peer-to-peer, non-custodially. Sablier does not include a marketplace layer. For more on OTC functionality, see Cryptool vs Whales.market.

Is cryptool non-custodial like sablier?

Yes. Cryptool is non-custodial. Wallets connect read-only for portfolio tracking. On-chain transactions are signed by the user's wallet, and funds never move through Cryptool. Sablier is also non-custodial: tokens sit in the vesting contract and release according to the schedule, with no intermediary.
